Posted a week ago, budget far below scope, client has never hired

fields.label: Dollar saving per win from boosting

task.explanation: Normal: 16 x 25 = 400 Connects per win. Boosted: 40 x 10 = 400. No saving: the decision then rests on other factors such as how fast you need wins or deal size.

prompt: It is the middle of the month and the team has used 70% of its monthly Connects budget, with no wins yet this month.

task.prompt: It is the middle of the month and the team has used 70% of its monthly Connects budget, with no wins yet this month.

steps.question: What is the first thing to check?
options: Stop bidding for the rest of the month
Buy more Connects immediately
Which jobs the Connects went to, and whether they matched the selection criteria
Whether a competitor has more Connects
steps.explanation: Before spending more, find out whether bids are going to poor-fit jobs or proposals are weak.

steps.question: You find half the bids went to jobs with 50+ proposals posted days earlier. What do you change?
options: Write longer proposals for those jobs
Lower your hourly rate
Tighten the rule: bid early on fresh, verified, good-fit jobs and skip stale crowded posts
Nothing, it is just bad luck
steps.explanation: Stale, crowded jobs have low odds; the fix is in selection, not price or length.

prompt: A BD lead proposed this monthly Connects plan. Mark the parts that would waste Connects or hurt results.

task.prompt: A BD lead proposed this monthly Connects plan. Mark the parts that would waste Connects or hurt results.

segments.text: Track Connects spent, interviews and wins per job category every week.
Boost every proposal, whatever the job, so we always appear at the top.
segments.issue: Boosting everything burns budget on poor-fit jobs; boost selectively where fit and value are high.

segments.text: Reserve part of the budget for high-value jobs that appear late in the month.
Send the same generic proposal to as many jobs as possible to maximise volume.
segments.issue: Generic volume bids lower win rate and waste Connects on proposals that cannot stand out.

segments.text: Review which categories return the most revenue per Connect and shift budget toward them.
Skip reading the client's history to save time.
segments.issue: Client history (payment, hires, reviews) is the main signal of whether a bid is worth it.

segments.text: Agree a monthly cap so spending is planned, not reactive.

prompt: Which metric best tells you whether Connects are being spent well?

options: Total number of proposals sent
Number of Connects bought this month
How many jobs were viewed
Revenue won per Connect (or per 100 Connects) by job category
mcq.explanation: Volume metrics say nothing about return; revenue per Connect ties spend directly to outcomes.

prompt: Why does bidding early on a fresh job usually give better return on Connects?

options: Early bids cost fewer Connects on every job
Late proposals are hidden from clients
Clients must hire from the first ten proposals
Clients often review the first proposals and start interviews before the list gets long
mcq.explanation: Clients tend to engage with early proposals; arriving after dozens of others lowers your odds. Avoid claiming platform rules that may change.

prompt: Boosted bids raise your interview rate but cost more. When is boosting most justified?

options: On low-budget jobs, because they are easy to win
Only on jobs that already have many proposals
On high-value, strong-fit jobs where the higher win odds outweigh the extra cost
On every job, to stay visible
mcq.explanation: Boost where expected value (win odds x deal size) rises more than the extra Connects cost.
